rationale: Used an isolated Codex implementation lane because the change combines durable artifact semantics, retention enforcement, container packaging, CI publication, and least-privilege Azure infrastructure.
Private-only ACR publication is restricted to a dedicated VNet-connected self-hosted runner, while deployment requires existing private-endpoint, private-DNS-link, and Container Apps subnet evidence.

Used separate independent runtime and infrastructure security reviews; both closed without blocking findings after bounded repairs. No live Azure resource, deployment, role assignment, database, or source endpoint was touched.

alternatives_rejected.reason: Azure Files mounting would require storage-account-key access and would not preserve the approved managed-identity-only storage boundary.
Platform lifecycle deletion cannot create the required content-free tombstone before deletion and could not preserve the governed crash-resume semantics.
Expiry tied only to a later acquisition rerun cannot guarantee the approved 30-day candidate and receipt retention.
The implementation changes security-sensitive storage, identity, deletion, and deployment boundaries and therefore requires independent review.
A GitHub-hosted runner has no authorized route to a public-network-disabled ACR and must not be used for publication.

escalation_history: Offline storage tests exposed and drove repairs for test imports and tombstone crash-resume behavior.
Bicep validation rejected the first multiline digest assertion; the expression was simplified and recompiled successfully.
The worker image build rejected host-generated Windows object artifacts; a tracked root .dockerignore now excludes host build outputs.
Overlapping long test runs caused one assembly-lock build failure; owned test processes were stopped and the final suite was rerun once from final no-build binaries with a complete passing TRX.
